Directly re-litigates the P051 abrogation that names Generate as an execute site.

Producer prop set is `{color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?}` (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts) — no `tag`. defects.mechanism: F1 — producer contract drift: glass-ui 7.0.0 landed the P051 removal while the consumer still writes the 6.x interactive-host idiom; Vue discards the unknown prop silently, so no typecheck, console warning or unit test fires.

defects.defect: The rail axis is mapped twice over two different boxes: the forward map (pointer -> position) is TypeScript over the BORDER box (getBoundingClientRect), while the inverse map (position -> pixels) is CSS calc where `100%` resolves against the PADDING box. They disagree by the 1px border at each end, so the two maps are not inverse.
defects.evidence: GradientStopEditor.vue:75-81 (forward: origin rect.left=224, span rect.width-20=442) vs :55-57 (inverse: `calc(10px + (100% - 20px) * p/100)` where 100%=460, origin=225). LIVE measured: rail x=224.0 width=462.0 borderLeft=1px; handle "Gradient stop at 0%" style.left="calc(0% + 10px)" measured centre cx=235; handle "…100%" style.left="calc(100% - 10px)" cx=675. Forward map at those exact pixels: pos(235)=0.226, pos(675)=99.774. LIVE confirmation: clicking the bar at x=235 — the exact pixel where the 0% handle is painted, at y=railTop+4 so the bar owns the gesture — minted a stop at 0.2%, rendered `style.left="calc(0.2% + 9.96px)"`, cx=235.88.

Error is antisymmetric: 0 at 50%, ±0.23% at the ends.
defects.proposedCure: A single useRailGeometry(el, halfPx) exposing toPosition(clientX) and toOffsetPx(position) over ONE box, built on clamp+scale from @mkbabb/value.js/math, with the handle positioned in px rather than calc(%) so the two directions are provably inverse. defects.defect: The self-declared "ONE sampling law" is implemented twice, and the model's interpolation space never reaches the emitted CSS. GradientVisualizer.colorAtPosition re-implements the interval walk / easing / mix that sampleCoalescedStops owns, then injects it into this component as an optional function prop — so the ghost dot and the rail it floats over are painted by two different implementations. Separately, rampGradient emits `linear-gradient(90deg, …)` with no `in <space>` clause, so the browser blends between sub-stops in sRGB while the model's law is oklch; COALESCE_RESOLUTION=32 exists to make that error small, i.e. the coalescing machinery is a polyfill for a CSS Color 4 feature the target browsers already ship.
defects.evidence: useGradientCSS.ts:171-174 declares "The ONE sampling law"; useGradientCSS.ts:175-216 implements it; GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 re-implements it and passes it as `:color-at` (GradientVisualizer.vue:139) into GradientStopEditor.vue:16. useGradientCSS.ts:223 `return \`linear-gradient(90deg, ${parts.join(", ")})\`` — no interpolation-space clause though model.interpolationSpace is in scope. Live computed --rail-ramp confirms: `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, …)`, no `in oklch`.
defects.mechanism: the concept "the colour of this ramp at position p" has no exported home, so it leaks into a component prop; and the model's declared interpolation space is dropped at the serialization boundary, forcing a 32-sample approximation of an exact platform feature
defects.reproduction: Structural — two call sites, both quoted with file:line. The sRGB-vs-oklch deviation between adjacent sub-stops is bounded by the 32-sample density and was NOT separately measured: that half is labelled a HYPOTHESIS.
defects.proposedCure: model/sample.ts exports both sampleAt(model, position) -> AnyColor (the ghost AND the bar-click mint) and sampleRamp(model); model/serialize.ts emits `linear-gradient(<dir> in <space>, …)` and coalesces ONLY across intervals whose easing is non-linear. Since parseGradientCSS seeds every parsed interval to the `linear` preset (gradientParse.ts:295-298), the common case collapses to an exact two-stop `linear-gradient(in oklch, …)`. The colorAt prop is deleted.

result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (claude-opus-5[1m], 1M-context arm) — the tier explicitly declared for this seat; declaration present and matched, not inherited, not undeclared.
result.strongestDefect: D-1 — the rail carries TWO different position axes: the ramp is painted across the full border-box (`background-size:100% 100%`, `serializeRailRamp` emits `linear-gradient(90deg,…)`) while handles/ghost/hit-maths ride an inset `[11, W-11]` track (`handleLeft`, `getPosition`, `HANDLE_HALF=10`). They agree only at 50%. Measured: the 0% swatch sits 11px = 2.38% of the ramp (desktop, W=462) / 3.40% (mobile, W=324) right of where the ramp paints 0%; a click at rail-fraction 12% mints a stop labelled 10% and 88% mints 90%. The file's own doc-comment (lines 8–13) asserts "handles, add-ghost and ramp share one axis by construction" — the exact opposite of what ships. This one mechanism explains the wrong ghost colour, the wrong minted colour, the wrong click→position map, and the end-of-rail dead bands.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as the seat's honest negative findings in §15 of the report: motion is fully tokenised and resolves (computed `box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), transform 0.44s linear(…)`, no ad-hoc durations, animates only transform/box-shadow — no layout-forcing property); prefers-reduced-motion is honoured by inheritance from glass-ui `dist/styles/utilities/a11y-overrides.css` whose `transition-property: opacity, color, background-color, border-color, box-shadow !important` outranks the inline shorthand and drops `transform` (measured `transitionDuration 0.1s` under reducedMotion:reduce); every token the file names resolves non-empty (`--spring-snappy-duration` = `calc(0.44s * 1)`, `--focus-ring-inner/-outer`, `--alpha-checker`, `--touch-target`, `--radius-pill`, `--shadow-sm`); the dual-contrast focus ring composes with `--shadow-sm` exactly as claimed; the visual REPORT's "20×20 small tap target" rows are a border-box measurement artefact — the real hit region is 24×24 on fine pointers (elementFromPoint sweep `hitSpanX [-12,11,24]`), so WCAG 2.5.8's minimum is met at rest; RTL correctly does not mirror per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2; zero console errors, zero page errors, zero horizontal overflow on /#/gradient across all four Safari matrices and all 11 probe runs; `verbatimModuleSyntax` and Vue 3.5 idiom (useTemplateRef, reactive props destructure) are clean. Evidence gap declared: WebKit does not implement forced-colors, so the shipped `forced-colors-desktop` matrix renders in full colour and the component's `@media (forced-colors: active)` block at :353–359 is UNTESTED — not claimed as a finding.

defects.defect: On touch, tapping inside a SELECTED stop handle's own advertised hit region DELETES the stop. The remove chip (top-11, 44px below the rail) carries the same always-on hit inflation (--touch-target 2.75rem = 44px) as the handle, and the selected handle's scale(1.25) also scales its ::before expander to 55px, so the two invisible regions overlap with the destructive one on top (chip z-20 vs handle z-10). No undo, no confirmation, no visual cue.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T11 (iPhone 14 context against http://localhost:9000/#/gradient)

This is the same transposition that cures D-4 and D-9. If a rail-local remove must survive, it goes on the opposite side of the rail from the drag axis and the two expanders are made mutually exclusive.

defects.defect: No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.

Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.

defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10
defects.proposedCure: The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

defects.defect: The instrument has two different position axes for one domain quantity. The ramp is painted across the full border-box; handles, the add-ghost and the pointer inverse ride an inset [HANDLE_HALF, W-HANDLE_HALF] track. They agree only at 50%. The file's own doc-comment asserts they 'share one axis by construction'.
defects.evidence: evidence/p1.mjs: `BAR x=224.00 w=462.00`, handle 'Gradient stop at 0%' `centerX=235.00` (ramp paints 0% at x=224), handle 'Gradient stop at 100%' `centerX=675.00` (ramp paints 100% at x=686) → 11px = 2.38% of the ramp. evidence/p5.mjs (iPhone 14): bar w=324, centres 44/346 → 11px = 3.40%. evidence/p3.mjs T6: ten clicks at rail fractions .12 .20 .28 .36 .44 .52 .60 .72 .80 .88 produce `pos ["0","10","19","27","35","44","52","60","73","81","90","100"]` — click at 12.0% mints 10%, click at 88.0% mints 90%. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:317-326 (.gradient-rail background-size 100% 100%, origin/clip border-box), useGradientCSS.ts:266 (linear-gradient(90deg,…)), GradientStopEditor.vue:55-57 (handleLeft), :75-81 (getPosition), :8-13 and :49-53 (the false claim).
defects.mechanism: two coordinate systems for one domain quantity, neither derived from the other
defects.reproduction: node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p1.mjs (geometry) and evidence/p3.mjs block T6 (click→position map)
defects.proposedCure: One axis, expressed once. Either paint the ramp on the inset track (background-position: 11px 0; background-size: calc(100% - 22px) 100% — the pill caps then hold flat terminal colour, which is what a 0%/100% stop actually means), or put the handles on the full-width axis and inset the rail's silhouette instead. HANDLE_HALF must be read from the rendered handle box rather than re-declared as a JS literal (D-13).

Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:288 (top-11, absolute), GradientVisualizer.vue:135 (flex flex-col gap-5 parent), :148 (the hr).

defects.mechanism: A design-system prop contract enforced by neither the type system nor the runtime. The producer may rename any prop and every consumer keeps compiling and keeps rendering something — worse than breaking, because it is invisible. Aggravated by glass-ui 7's own internal inconsistency: Slider and Badge kept `variant`, only Button moved to `emphasis`.
defects.reproduction: Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: "Regenerate" and the two icon buttons beside it render at IDENTICAL pale weight — three default-emphasis buttons, not one saturated primary flanked by two ghosts. defects.proposedCure: Producer-first, and it belongs in the Glass 8 release gate (G-3), not a 51-site consumer sweep that rots on the next rename: glass-ui closes ButtonProps to unknown attributes, or asserts in dev when a `variant` attr reaches a Button root. Acceptance: `<Button variant="ghost">` FAILS at typecheck or first render, reproducibly in CI. Secondarily reconcile the axis naming across Button/Slider/Badge, since the inconsistency is what made 51 sites wrong by default. Only then sweep the consumers (variant="primary-audacious" → emphasis="primary", variant="ghost" → emphasis="quiet"), leaving Slider/Badge `variant` untouched.

defects.defect: `demo/ui/` is a nineteen-directory pure re-export alias layer over @mkbabb/glass-ui — the forbidden legacy shim surface. GenerateControls crosses it four times, and the file simultaneously uses three different specifier registers for one package.
defects.evidence: All 19 of 19 subdirs are shim-only: `for f in demo/ui/*/index.ts; do [ -z "$(ls $(dirname $f) | grep -v '^index.ts$')' ] && echo SHIM-ONLY; done` lists all nineteen. `cat demo/ui/button/index.ts` → `export { Button } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` (entire file); select/slider/badge/card identical in form. GenerateControls.vue:3-12 imports via the shims, :14 via the glass-ui root barrel directly, :15 via the granular subpath — three registers in twelve lines. glass-ui publishes 74 subpaths; this file uses one.
defects.mechanism: A migration that stopped one step short of the root: the shadcn tree was kept alive as an alias surface. Violates edict 2 (no aliases/shims/dual paths) and edict 3 (no wrapper layers that need not exist), at directory scale. It also actively hides which design system and which version a call site binds to — the proximate reason L-0 went unnoticed.

Honest scoping: glass-ui declares sideEffects:["*.css"] and its root barrel imports no CSS, so Rollup can tree-shake it — I measured no production bundle penalty and do not claim one. The defect is structural and legibility, not perf.
defects.proposedCure: Delete demo/ui/ entirely; import each component from its granular glass-ui subpath (@mkbabb/glass-ui/button, /select, /slider, /badge, /card). One specifier form, one hop, the version and prop vocabulary visible at every call site. CURABLE NOW for the ten other consumers; BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 for this file's four lines.

defects.defect: Library-shaped code stranded in the demo: the library owns palette EXTRACTION (quantize) but not palette SYNTHESIS. demo/color-session/generate-color.ts is 243 lines of pure, Vue-free, DOM-free, seeded color math whose only outside calls are three published value.js primitives — structurally indistinguishable from src/quantize.ts, which IS published.

The demo exists to dogfood the library; instead it privately owns a capability the library should publish, so no consumer can reach it and no published type describes it. Nearly half the library test suite is testing demo modules because those modules are unpromoted library code.

defects.defect: The demo's proof of the published subpath surface is not a proof. tsconfig.demo.json's hand-rolled `paths` block has drifted from package.json#exports in BOTH directions — 3 phantom entries pointing at nonexistent .d.ts files and rejected by Node, and 2 real published subpaths left unmapped — and where they overlap, `paths` substitution means TypeScript never consults the exports map at all.

In tsconfig but NOT exported: /parsing, /units, and the bare root. Exported but NOT in tsconfig: /value, /css. `node --input-type=module -e "await import(…)"` → `@mkbabb/value.js` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/parsing` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/units` ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED, `/css` RESOLVED, `/color` RESOLVED. `test -f dist/index.d.ts || echo MISSING` → MISSING; same for dist/subpaths/parsing.d.ts and units.d.ts. The comment at tsconfig.demo.json:37-41 is false three ways: it claims a bare `.` root (absent), a "CLOSED 8-key set" (it is 7), and that it "Mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map" (it does not).

Delete "./color" from exports and the demo typecheck stays GREEN while every real consumer breaks at install — the demo's 25 /color imports are therefore not a proof of the published surface.

Prior seat additionally captured `tsc --traceResolution` showing two imports in the SAME file (generate-color.ts) resolving by two different mechanisms: /color via paths substitution with no Package ID, /css via "Entering conditional exports" with Package ID @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0.

Self-reference resolution already works (the /css trace proves it, with a real Package ID), so all seven subpaths would resolve through the genuine exports map and removing a subpath would turn the demo typecheck RED — which is what a dogfood is for. If a paths block must survive, generate it from package.json#exports the way Vite does. Add one test/dist/ gate asserting Object.keys(exports) ≡ the resolvable specifier set.

defects.defect: The shell→feature action seam is five hops of `any` and double optional-chain masking: the dock action bar reaches into this component's instance by name to invoke Regenerate/Save/Copy.
defects.evidence: Chain: demo/color-picker/App.vue:317 `const generatePaneRef = ref<any>(null)` → demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:106-110 `interface PaneActionRefs { generate: Ref<any>; gradient: Ref<any>; mix: Ref<any> }` → usePaneRouter.ts:196-198 `handler: () => paneRefs.generate.value?.regenerate?.()` → GeneratePane.vue:23-25 `regenerate: () => controlsRef.value?.regenerate?.()` → GenerateControls.vue:115 `defineExpose({ regenerate, save, copyColors })`. Those three Ref<any> are the ONLY `any` in usePaneRouter.ts (`grep -n 'any' demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts` → lines 108, 109, 110 only).
defects.mechanism: Ownership, not typing. useColorGeneration() is instantiated INSIDE GenerateControls (:35-42), so generation state is owned by a component instance and the shell has no way to reach it except by grabbing the instance. The `any` is the symptom; the state's home is the disease. The `?.` on the METHOD (as distinct from the instance) exists only to swallow a contract mismatch — a masking fallback in the sense edict 2 forbids: rename `regenerate` anywhere in the chain and the dock button silently no-ops with no type error, no runtime error, no console warning.
defects.reproduction: Read the five sites above. The same three verbs are ALSO rendered declaratively on the plate (:157-184), so one concept has both a declarative and an imperative path and only the imperative one can break silently.
defects.proposedCure: Invert it. useColorGeneration becomes a pane-scoped session provided by GeneratePane under a typed InjectionKey — the pattern already used in this very tree (CSS_COLOR_KEY, LIBRARY_PORT_KEY, EDIT_TARGET_KEY). The pane declares its action descriptors as typed DATA ({key, icon, title, handler}[]) and hands them to the router, which injects rather than reaches. PaneActionRefs, both defineExpose blocks, controlsRef, App.vue's three ref<any>, and all six ?. masks delete. Pays three times: elegance, correctness (L-1 becomes unrepresentable — save reads the name from the same session the input writes), and performance (session computeds replace per-render template calls, L-9).

defects.defect: The dropdown preview cost claim ("10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond") holds at the default count 5 and fails by 2.8× at count 12; the two truth functions are plain template calls, not computeds, so every re-render of the mounted SelectContent recomputes all sixteen strips.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:88-93 carries the claim. Prior seat measured the bundled core on node/V8: one generatePalette(count=5) 0.097ms; count=12 0.362ms; preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=5 = 0.871ms (claim HOLDS); preset dropdown open 10 strips @count=12 = 2.80ms (claim FAILS). presetStops/harmonyStops at :94-100 are plain function calls — Vue memoizes neither. PreviewStrip caps at 7 segments (STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP, a PRIVATE constant in PreviewStrip.vue), so at count 12 the host pays to generate five colors the chip discards; the sibling RAMP form does publish its budget (RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT is exported from color-chips/sample.ts and re-exported from the barrel).
defects.mechanism: Asymmetric public surface in the chip module — the ramp tells hosts its sampling budget, the strip hides it — so the host cannot size its truth function honestly. Desktop-V8 numbers; WebKit on the mobile matrix would be materially slower, putting a count-12 dropdown open into multi-frame territory.
defects.reproduction: Bundle demo/color-session/generate-color.ts with esbuild and time generatePalette across counts; read PreviewStrip.vue for the private cap and color-chips/sample.ts for the exported RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT.
defects.proposedCure: NOT "generate only 7" — generateHues for `analogous` derives its step from count, so a 7-generation is not the prefix of a 12-generation and truncating would break the seed-exactness law the file rightly insists on. Instead: export STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP so the host can decide honestly, and wrap the two truth functions in computeds keyed on (count, preset, harmony, seed) — which the L-6 session transposition delivers for free.

defects.defect: "Palette stops → CSS rail" is hand-rolled in four places with no owner, the markup sandwich is duplicated verbatim across two workbenches, and the mechanism violates the shared chip module's own SAMPLING LAW — visibly, in the same card.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:65-73 and demo/workbenches/extract/composables/useExtractSession.ts:101-112 are near-byte twins: same `length===0 → "var(--muted)"` guard, same `length===1?50:(i/(len-1))*100`, same `.toFixed(0)`, same `linear-gradient(to right, ${stops.join(", ")})`. Two more copies at demo/workbenches/mix/MixResultDisplay.vue:112 and demo/picker/controls/ComponentSliders/ComponentSliders.vue:195. The MARKUP is duplicated too: GenerateControls.vue:292-307 vs ExtractControls.vue:18-33 are character-identical on the structural lines (`relative flex-1 h-6 flex items-center` wrapper, `absolute inset-0 rounded-full overflow-hidden h-6` rail div, `Slider variant="spectrum" class="relative w-full"`, `:style="{ '--slider-track-bg': 'transparent' }"`). That last line is a per-instance override of a design-system token, which edict 5 forbids by name; `grep -rn -- '--slider-track-bg' demo/` finds 4 override sites. demo/color-session/color-chips/sample.ts:5-12 legislates the opposite: "ramps are k-sample discrete stops built from THE LIBRARY's mixColors interpolation — NEVER CSS `in <space>` gradient interpolation, because the preview must show what THE APP computes, not what the browser's engine would … One mechanism for all rows, no engine divergence."
defects.mechanism: The concept "a slider whose track IS a color ramp" has no home, so it lives four times in demo features and zero times in the design system that owns Slider. The component then runs TWO contradictory mechanisms for "show a color sequence" — the law-abiding library-sampled PreviewStrip in its dropdowns (:245, :274) and the forbidden raw CSS gradient in its slider track (:72), eleven lines above the import of the module that forbids it.
defects.reproduction: Visible in shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: the plate strip shows five clean hard segments (green·lavender·gold·cyan·pink) while the count slider directly below shows the browser's sRGB interpolation between them — the muddy grey-green between green and lavender is a color the app never computed. The instrument and its readout disagree in the same card. Confirm the duplication with `grep -rn 'linear-gradient(to right' demo/`.
defects.proposedCure: BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 (G-2): the rail belongs in glass-ui as a first-class affordance on the existing Slider — a `trackStops: readonly string[]` prop or a `track` slot — with sampling routed through color-chips/sample.ts so the slider obeys the same SAMPLING LAW as the chips and the visible engine divergence disappears. Both workbenches then delete their rail div, their --slider-track-bg override, and their gradient computed; the whole idiom collapses to `<Slider :track-stops="stops" />`.

defects.defect: `.generate-swatch` is a per-component class hook whose only rules are hand-added to two global selector lists that already carry the general seam `[data-color-surface]`.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue (glass BJ W4 pinned consumer; no source edits authorized)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id claude-opus-5[1m]. Spawned with an explicit Opus 5 declaration; served tier matches. Not an inherited or undeclared seat.
result.strongestDefect: C-1 — the per-swatch copy verb does not exist in the shipped build. GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes tag="button", :aria-label and @click to glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which declares 6 props (no `tag`), no emits, sets inheritAttrs:false and hand-forwards ONLY class/style, then renders a hardcoded <span aria-hidden="true"> with inline pointer-events:none that wins the style merge. Live DOM: tag=SPAN, ariaHidden=true, ariaLabel=null, tabIndex=-1, pointerEvents=none; the plate has exactly 4 tabbables and the 5 swatches contribute zero. copyColor() is unreachable dead code, and the code comment at :190-197 asserts the opposite in writing. An API break absorbed silently at the W44 Glass-7 adoption because unknown attrs are legal Vue fallthrough and invisible to every gate.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded as the audited-and-clean surface so no seat invents these: (1) NO ungated rAF — WatercolorDot is mounted without `animate` (default false) and the compiled useWatercolorBlob returns before registering its rAF (`if (l.value = …, !a) return {borderRadius,transform}` precedes `t(e=>g(e.now),…)`); even when armed the loop declares {pauseWhenHidden:true, respectReducedMotion:true}. (2) Nothing to clean up — no listeners, observers, timers, subscriptions or imperative DOM; only async is the two clipboard awaits; palette is a computed over four refs, no unbounded growth. (3) No defineModel stale-read hazard — the sole v-model is on a native <input> bound to a local ref, which is the prescribed synchronous-cache shape. (4) No ValueUnit nesting, no oklch→HSV/stableHue surface, no WebGL, no parseCssColor call — the component only emits strings the library serialized, and generatedCss checks .ok on all three of oklch/mapColorToGamut/serializeCssColor. (5) The T-17 seed-exactness law genuinely HOLDS: presetStops(c) === generatePalette(count,c,harmony,seed) and selecting c computes the identical call; mulberry32 is deterministic; the O-20 failure diff is numerically equal on all five rows (85.53637546394% ≡ 0.855364), i.e. a string-form artefact, not a lying preview. (6) The comment's "zero rest cost" half is TRUE — measured document.querySelectorAll('[data-stops]').length === 0 with both Selects closed. (7) verbatimModuleSyntax clean — all four type-only imports are `import type`. (8) No god module, no legacy shims/aliases/dual paths, no contrived shared dirs, no deleted animations. (9) Edict 5 NOT violated by `--slider-track-bg` — it is a producer-sanctioned token read with fallback in glass-ui.css (`--slider-track-bg,var(--muted-medium`), and the BJ W4 hold plans to rename that exact seam at v8. (10) Pin verified: shasum -a 256 → 4f95c57c7a6c46fa15a08b98b954a39529a12f71bda672423c7008c33ae324f6, matches CARRY-LEDGER §D exactly, no coordination-boundary drift.

defects.defect: The per-swatch copy verb is entirely dead: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` are all silently discarded by glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which renders a hardcoded aria-hidden span with pointer-events:none. The swatches are not buttons, have no accessible name, are not focusable, and cannot be clicked; copyColor() is unreachable.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:199-208 (the four bindings) · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/watercolor-dot/WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts:23-52 declares {color,variant?,animate?,cycleDuration?,range?,seed?} and no emits · `grep -o "tag" node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js | wc -l` → 0 · watercolor-dot.js setup body: `inheritAttrs:!1` with `n=h(), c=i(()=>n.class), f=i(()=>n.style)` (class/style only) and root `<span aria-hidden="true" style=[attrs, {backgroundColor, borderRadius, pointerEvents:"none", …}]>` · LIVE DOM at http://localhost:9000/#/generate: {"tag":"SPAN","ariaHidden":"true","ariaLabel":null,"tabIndex":-1,"tagAttr":null,"pointerEvents":"none","cursor":"pointer","w":40,"h":40} and tabbablesInPlate = [INPUT "Palette name", BUTTON "Regenerate", BUTTON "Save palette", BUTTON "Copy all colors"] — the 5 swatches contribute 0
defects.mechanism: Producer/consumer contract break absorbed by Vue's legal-fallthrough semantics: a component with inheritAttrs:false that hand-forwards a whitelist of attrs silently swallows every unlisted attr AND every listener, and the type system treats unknown attributes on a component as valid fallthrough. The consumer's documented idiom (tag="button") was never a prop.
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → click any colour swatch inside [data-generate-plate] → nothing is copied, no focus moves, no state changes. Structurally: the DOM dump above (SPAN / aria-hidden=true / pointer-events:none / tabIndex -1 / aria-label null).
defects.proposedCure: The dot is a FACE, not a SEAT. Transpose rather than patch: a real <button> seat wraps the dot (dot stays the decorative aria-hidden child it was built to be; the button carries name, focus affordance, ≥24px target, listener). Better for a 9-consumer species: glass-ui grows the seat — a WatercolorDotButton, or an explicit as/tag + attr-forwarding contract on WatercolorDot. Relay R-1 to the glass BH inbox; the consumer half is BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8. Do NOT delete the three dead bindings — that retires the verb, not the defect.

defects.defect: Gate vacuity, three ways: the component's ONLY oracle (O-20) is currently RED for an unrelated serialization-form reason, CI never runs e2e at all, there are zero unit tests for the generation core, and `npm run typecheck` is green over every defect here.
defects.evidence: `npx playwright test e2e/smoke/oracles/o20-generate-plate.spec.ts --reporter=line` → "1 failed, 1 passed (39.2s)", failing at o20:105 with stamped "oklch(85.53637546394% 0.087179123785 49.783647190779deg)" vs live "oklch(0.855364 0.0871791 49.7836)" (numerically IDENTICAL — serializeCssColor vs getComputedStyle forms) · `grep -n "run:" .github/workflows/ci.yml` → npm ci / lint / vue-tsc lib / vue-tsc demo / build / npm test / verify-packed-surface / tsc / npm test — no playwright step in any of ci.yml, deploy-pages.yml, release.yml · `grep -rln "GenerateControls|useColorGeneration|generatePalette|generateSingleColor" test e2e` → only o20-generate-plate.spec.ts · `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit; echo EXIT=$?` → EXIT=0 with --listFiles confirming both GenerateControls.vue and WatercolorDot.vue.d.ts in the program · o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts:33-41 pins its WCAG-2.5.8 BR-3 rule to openGradient() only
defects.mechanism: Oracles assert decorative properties (a forwarded class + computed backgroundColor) instead of the control contract (role, accessible name, operability), so they are indifferent to whether the control exists; and the one oracle that would fail is neither run by CI nor currently green.
defects.reproduction: MUTATION TEST — delete `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` from GenerateControls.vue:199-208 and re-run O-20: the result is unchanged (test 1 still passes, test 2 still fails for its own serialization reason). o20:98-105 selects `.generate-swatch` (a class WatercolorDot DOES forward) and reads getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor (painted by the producer regardless).
defects.proposedCure: Assert the contract, not the paint: O-20's swatch leg becomes role + accessible-name assertions; its byte-identity leg normalises both sides through one serializer. Generalise o27-focus-affordance.spec.ts from openGradient() to the route matrix so BR-3 (≥24px) and the focus-affordance rules cover every route. Put test:e2e in ci.yml or delete the suite — an unrun oracle manufactures the false confidence that let a 7.0.0 API break reach the shipped plate. All three land in e2e/ and touch no pinned consumer.

defects.defect: The plate's editable name is discarded on save — renaming the palette has no effect. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]`; the only consumer declares a one-parameter handler and hardcodes the literal "Generated Palette".
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:48-50 (`defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`) and :102-104 (`emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`) · demo/workbenches/generate/GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)` · demo/palettes/usePaletteStore.ts:66 `function createPalette(name: string, colors: PaletteColor[])` — the name parameter exists and is ignored · LIVE: {"inputValueAfter":"MY UNIQUE NAME 4711", "namesBefore":["Generated Palette","Sunset",…], "namesAfter":["Generated Palette","Generated Palette","Sunset",…]}
defects.mechanism: Positional emit payload silently dropped by handler arity — TypeScript accepts a narrower handler as assignable to a wider emit signature, so vue-tsc cannot see the drop. The same drop applies to the dock-driven save (GeneratePane.vue:22-26 re-exposes save through the same emit).
defects.reproduction: http://localhost:9000/#/generate → type any name into the plate title input → click the Save-palette button → read localStorage["color-palettes"]: the new entry is named "Generated Palette", not the typed name. Verified live with a native value setter + input event so v-model commits.
defects.proposedCure: Immediate: bind the payload — `onSave(colors: string[], name: string)` → `pm.createPalette(name, paletteColors)`. Structural cure that kills the class: emit a single object payload (`save: [{ colors, name }]`) so ignoring a field must be explicit rather than a consequence of arity. (GeneratePane.vue is not the pinned file, but no source edits land from this formation — authored as a wave item.)

defects.defect: The generated palette — the workbench's entire output — has zero accessible representation, and none of the three verbs announces anything.
defects.evidence: PaletteColorStrip.vue:2-10 aria-hidden="true" role="presentation" · the swatches are producer-hardcoded aria-hidden with the :aria-label discarded (C-1) · PreviewStrip.vue:43 aria-hidden="true" · GenerateControls.vue:293-296 the count ramp is an unlabelled decorative div · LIVE probe of every live region on the page while operating the plate: [{"role":"alert","live":null,"text":"dev misconfigured — run `npm run dev`"}] — that is the dev banner; there is no status seat

Compounded by no aria-live for the async/replacing results.

Give the PALETTE a text alternative once, at region level: the <section>'s accessible name carries count + ordered colours, or a visually-hidden <ul> of the css strings that doubles as the keyboard seat for C-1's copy verbs (one structure, both cures). Add exactly one role="status" in the plate that regenerate, save and both copies write to — which also discharges C-6 and C-12.

defects.defect: Both clipboard call sites await `writeClipboard` and discard the discriminated result the producer designed to be read, so a denied or hung copy is indistinguishable from a successful one.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/generate/GenerateControls.vue:106-113 — `await writeClipboard(palette.value.join(", "))` and `await writeClipboard(css)`, both results dropped · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts:16-37 — `export type CopyResult = { ok: true } | { ok: false; reason: CopyFailureReason }` with the doc comment "Returns the discriminated result … rather than a lossy boolean, for identical call ergonomics: `const { ok } = await writeClipboard(text)`" · the producer also ships useClipboard({status, copy}) with scope-owned confirmation state

defects.reproduction: NONE from the shipped happy path — the drop is source-dispositive (GenerateControls.vue:107 and :112 discard the return). Combined with C-3 (no live region) neither success nor failure produces any user-perceivable signal, so 'Copy all colors' is already indistinguishable from a no-op today.

defects.defect: The code comment's own performance claim is false by measurement: the preset dropdown's seed-exact previews cost 1.3 ms at count 5 and 3.6 ms at count 12, not 'sub-millisecond'.

defects.defect: The plate-chrome row wraps at the DEFAULT desktop pane width, not at 390 as the source comment documents — so the intended one-line composition (name — count — regenerate — actions) never renders at any viewport.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:138-142 claims "at 390 the verbs settle onto their own right-aligned line" · docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png shows the verb cluster already on its own second line at desktop with a wide dead gap beside the title · flex base sizes at the measured pane (content ≈ 437 CSS px): input basis-[10rem]=160 + badge ≈34 + cluster (Regenerate 145 + Save 36 + Copy 36 + 2 inner gaps) = 233 + 2 row gaps = 443 > 437

defects.defect: The editable palette name's only affordance is `hover:underline`, which does not exist on touch — on mobile the field is visually indistinguishable from a heading, and there is no placeholder for the emptied state.

result.strongestDefect: L2-1 — the five per-swatch copy verbs on the Generate plate DO NOT EXIST in the product. GenerateControls.vue:199-208 passes `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` to `<WatercolorDot>`, but glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot declares only `color|variant|animate|cycleDuration|range|seed`, ships `inheritAttrs:false`, and hardcodes `aria-hidden="true"`. Measured live: the rendered element is a SPAN with no tag/aria-label/role/tabindex; `.focus()` leaves `document.activeElement===swatch` false; `.click()` produces ZERO clipboard writes while the positive control ("Copy all colors") produces one. Three gates are green over it — `vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json` EXIT=0, the O-20 oracle asserts only `backgroundColor`, and the visual audit's interactive-element probe cannot see an aria-hidden span. This is the third member of the same producer-surface disease pass 1 found on `<Button variant>` (§L-0), and the first with a FUNCTIONAL rather than cosmetic consequence — which is why the Glass 8 gate G-3 must widen from Button-only to any-unknown-attr-on-any-glass-ui-root.

defects.defect: The palette name the user types is silently discarded on save: the child emits `save: [colors, name]` but the pane's handler declares arity 1 and passes the literal "Generated Palette" to the persistence port. Data loss on user input.
defects.evidence: GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`, :52 `paletteName = ref("Generated Palette")`, :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — name parameter never bound — and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. LIVE REPRODUCTION (pass 2, which pass 1 had to abandon under shared-browser contention): {"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/generate","inputAfterSet":"ZZ-PROBE-NAME","nameMatches":[["color-palettes",["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"]]]} — the v-model round-trip is verified and the persisted store contains zero occurrences of ZZ-PROBE-NAME. Comment at :44-47 asserts 'this emit is already truthful' — it is not.
defects.mechanism: Ownership split with an untyped joint: the NAME is owned by the leaf component, the PERSISTENCE PORT (LIBRARY_PORT_KEY) is injected by the parent, and the two are joined by a Vue emit. TypeScript cannot catch it — a handler is always assignable to an emit with more parameters. Second symptom of the same split: `string[] → PaletteColor[]` is synthesised twice (GenerateControls.vue:55-57 and GeneratePane.vue:15-18) because neither file owns 'the generated palette as a domain object'.
defects.reproduction: Playwright at /#/generate with the self-healing hash idiom: set input[aria-label="Palette name"] to ZZ-PROBE-NAME via the native value setter + input event (verified round-trip), click button[aria-label="Save palette"], read localStorage['color-palettes'] → names are ["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"].
defects.proposedCure: ESCALATION RECOMMENDED — this is the highest-value action available before Glass 8. GeneratePane.vue is NOT in the hold's pinned receiver set (the four pinned files are ComponentSliders.vue, ConfigSliderPane.vue, ExtractControls.vue, GenerateControls.vue), so binding the second emit argument at GeneratePane.vue:14-19 cures the data loss WITHOUT touching any pinned file. The full cure is the session hoist: `useGenerateSession()` owning preset/harmony/count/seed/name/palette/regenerate/save, provided at the pane under a typed InjectionKey — one writer, one adapter, and the name-drop becomes unrepresentable.

result.axis: CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, direction of dependency, public surface)
result.modelObserved: Opus 5 (1M context) — exact model id `claude-opus-5[1m]`; the tier this seat was explicitly spawned with, declared not inherited.
result.strongestDefect: L-1 + L-2 read together: value.js has ceded ownership of its own easing vocabulary to its design system. At the package level `@mkbabb/glass-ui` (5.2M) and `@mkbabb/keyframes.js` (608K) are the ONLY entries in `package.json#dependencies` (lines 82-85) while `src/` and `dist/` reference them ZERO times and glass-ui peer-depends back on `@mkbabb/value.js@^4.0.0` — a declared package cycle costing every library consumer 5.8 MB. At the type level the same inversion appears as `useGradientModel.ts:49 export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue` — a Vue picker's v-model payload becomes the data contract of `gradientParse.ts`, a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it. Both cures are one edit in two places: value.js `/easing` mints `AuthoredEasing` + `serializeTimingFunction`, glass-ui narrows to them, `dependencies` empties — and L-3, L-4 and the duplicated literal minters dissolve rather than get patched.
result.negativeProof: Not applicable to the verdict (DEFECTIVE), but recorded so the absences are not re-litigated: (1) the premise's most-predicted defect is ABSENT — `grep -rn "@src" demo/workbenches/gradient/ | wc -l` → 0; every library import in this component's chain is a published subpath (`@mkbabb/value.js/easing`, `/color`, `/css`) that a real consumer could write, so the demo is a true proof of the public API here. (2) `package.json#exports` has no `"."` entry and nothing in src/demo/test/e2e imports bare `@mkbabb/value.js` — consistent, not a gap. (3) verbatimModuleSyntax: all three type-only imports in the subject (lines 30, 34, 36-40) are `import type`. (4) Visual audit `/#/gradient` × 4 Safari matrices: pageErrors 0, consoleErrors 0, overflowX 0, main 1 (REPORT.md:125,140,155,170); the 12 `bleeding` rows are the FadingScroll `width:max-content` strip by design; the 6 smallTapTargets and 1 namelessButton belong to the slug bar / stop handles / shell, not this component — its `.rail-btn` is exactly 24x24 CSS px, clearing the probe's `<24` filter and sitting on the WCAG 2.5.8 floor. The screenshot renders correctly.

defects.defect: The published library declares its own demo's design system as a runtime dependency, forming a declared package cycle and forcing 5.8 MB of unused install weight on every consumer.

Measured: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" dist/subpaths/*.js dist/value.js | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" demo/ | wc -l` → 0 (referenced by NOTHING in the repo). `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M + 608K, against dist/subpaths at 132K. glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes `"@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0"`.

defects.reproduction: `npm i @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` in an empty non-Vue project: the install pulls a Vue design system plus a keyframes engine and glass-ui's own peer set (vue, reka-ui, embla-carousel, tailwindcss, @mkbabb/pencil-boil). `import { CubicBezier } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"` uses none of them.
defects.proposedCure: Move both entries to `devDependencies`. `dependencies` becomes `{}` — the honest shape for a zero-runtime-dependency value library. Nothing breaks: `"files": ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages", …]` (package.json:49-53) never ships the demo.

defects.defect: The gradient domain model — including a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it — is typed by a Vue component's v-model payload imported from the design system.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:49 `export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;` (imported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing` at line 12). glass-ui's own declaration calls it "The picker's v-model payload" (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts). It propagates into UI-free code: gradientParse.ts:41 `interface ParsedGradientModel { …; intervals: GradientInterval[] }` (that module has zero Vue imports); useGradientCSS.ts:53-62,120-133,232-254; and the subject's own public contract GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, value: EasingPickerValue]`.
defects.mechanism: inverted semantic ownership: the concept 'an authored easing curve = mode + re-parseable CSS literal + resolved callable + raw params' is a value.js concept, but value.js publishes no such record, so its own demo borrows one from a package that depends on it.
defects.reproduction: NONE (latent). Failure scenario: glass-ui 8 renames `term`→`jump` or makes `points` optional for steps mode — a semver-legal design-system component change. That silently breaks value.js's headless gradient CSS parser, its serializers and its persisted model shape, none of which involve a picker.
defects.proposedCure: value.js `/easing` mints the record: `export interface AuthoredEasing { readonly mode: "bezier"|"steps"; readonly css: string; readonly fn: EasingFunction; readonly points: readonly [number,number,number,number]; readonly steps: number; readonly term: JumpPosition }`. Then `GradientInterval = AuthoredEasing` (no glass-ui import in the model at all) and glass-ui narrows to `export type EasingPickerValue = AuthoredEasing` — consuming the library's vocabulary, the direction its peerDeps already declare. The glass-ui type imports at useGradientModel.ts:12, easingCatalogue.ts:31-35 and GradientEasingEditor.vue:30 all collapse to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`.

defects.defect: The public surface parses CSS timing functions but cannot serialize one, so the demo hand-mints the literal and must stay byte-identical with a private glass-ui implementation — held in agreement by a comment.
defects.evidence: `grep -rn "export function serialize|export const serialize" src/css/ src/easing.ts` → serializeCssColor, serializeKeyframeSelector, serializeCssValue, serializeTimelineOptions — no timing-function serializer, while `/css` exports `parseTimingFunction` (src/subpaths/css.ts). Consequence at easingCatalogue.ts:38-56: comment says "glass-ui `useEasingPicker.readout` mints … MUST be byte-identical", then `bezierLiteral` re-implements `+n.toFixed(3)` joined by `", "` and `stepsLiteral` re-implements `steps(${n}, ${term})`.
defects.mechanism: asymmetric public surface (parse without serialize) forces a duplicate implementation of one CSS serialization law into a consumer, coupled to the original only by prose.
defects.reproduction: Deterministic from source: change glass-ui's `readout` join from `", "` to `","`. `bezierLiteral` still emits `", "`. The identity match at easingCatalogue.ts:220 (`SPECIMEN_TILES.find(t => t.css === interval.css)`) is a string compare, so it returns undefined, `tileIdFor` returns null, `specimenNameFor` (line 229) returns "custom" — all 30 bezier tiles render unpressed and every closed specimen row's head reads `custom` for a named preset, with no error raised anywhere.
defects.proposedCure: Add `serializeTimingFunction(ast: CssTimingFunction): string` to `src/css/`, exported from `/css` as the exact inverse of `parseTimingFunction`, round-trip tested in the existing test/bbnf-equivalence idiom. `bezierLiteral`/`stepsLiteral` delete; glass-ui's private minter delegates. One law, one home, provable by round-trip instead of by comment.

defects.defect: value.js declares the jump-term union and the jump-term array independently; glass-ui derives its name from the array; the demo casts across them — and any divergence detonates as a module-scope throw that kills the whole gradient chunk.
defects.evidence: src/easing.ts:13 `export type JumpPosition = "jump-start"|"jump-end"|"jump-none"|"jump-both";` and src/easing.ts:68 `export const jumpTerms = ["jump-start","jump-end","jump-none","jump-both"] as const;` — no derivation between them. glass-ui: `export type JumpTerm = (typeof jumpTerms)[number]`. Bridge cast at easingCatalogue.ts:136 `const position = term as JumpPosition;`. Runtime guard at src/easing.ts:136 returns `err({code:"jump_position_invalid"})`; easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 `easingValue` converts an err Result to a `throw`. The catalogue is built at module scope: easingCatalogue.ts:198 `export const SPECIMEN_FAMILIES = buildFamilies();`.
defects.mechanism: two hand-written declarations of one enum with no structural link, bridged by an unchecked cast at the consumer, guarding an eager module-scope evaluation.
defects.reproduction: Add "jump-middle" to `jumpTerms` (src/easing.ts:68) and forget `JumpPosition` (line 13). glass-ui's `JumpTerm` widens automatically and the picker offers the term; a `stepsTile` receives it; `steppedEase` returns err; `easingValue` throws during import evaluation of easingCatalogue.ts — a static import of GradientEasingEditor.vue → GradientVisualizer.vue → the async GradientPane chunk (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74). The entire gradient workbench fails to load from a one-line library edit.
defects.proposedCure: Delete the hand-written union: `export type JumpPosition = (typeof jumpTerms)[number];`. One declaration, mechanically derived; the cast at easingCatalogue.ts:136 deletes; divergence becomes impossible.

defects.defect: Interval identity is positional while stop identity is id-based, and the two are synced across modules by a length-only watcher that appends/truncates at the end — so inserting or removing a stop silently reassigns authored curves to the wrong stop pairs.
defects.evidence: useGradientModel.ts:33-37 (GradientStop has `id`); intervals have none. useGradientModel.ts:89-100 `watch(() => stops.value.length, len => { …intervals.value.push(linearInterval()); … intervals.value.length = needed })` — told only THAT the length changed, never WHERE. `removeStop` (122-125) removes by id from anywhere. `addStop` (116-120) sorts by position so an inserted stop can land first. The subject cements the ordinal contract: GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, …]` → useGradientModel.ts:134-140 `updateInterval(index, value)`.
defects.mechanism: a shadow array with no modelled identity, kept in size by a length signal that carries no positional information, in a different module from the identity-bearing collection it shadows.
defects.reproduction: Source-derived (all three sites quoted in the report). 1) initial `stops=[A@0%,B@100%]`, `intervals=[linear]` (useGradientModel.ts:79-83). 2) press `ease-out-back` on row `1 → 2` → `updateInterval(0,…)` → `intervals=[back]`. 3) click the rail near 0% → GradientVisualizer.vue:91 `addStop(...)` → sorted, new stop lands FIRST. 4) watcher sees len 2→3 and pushes `linearInterval()` at the END → `intervals=[back, linear]`. 5) `back`, authored for A→B, is now interval 0 = N→A; A→B is linear. Symmetrically `removeStop(firstStopId)` drops the LAST interval, shifting every curve one pair left; the specimen rows relabel (useSpecimenRows.ts:61) and report the wrong assignment as truth. Live confirmation was ABANDONED — the shared dev browser at :9000 is under concurrent control by other seats (the page self-navigated /#/gradient → /#/extract → /#/atmosphere mid-evaluate; other seats' ?probe=4 / ?probe=6 params observed) and the probe-parsimony edict applies.
defects.proposedCure: Architectural transposition: the easing belongs to the LEADING STOP, not a parallel array — `interface GradientStop { id; cssColor; position; easing: AuthoredEasing }` (the last stop's easing is simply unused). The length watcher DELETES; add/remove become identity-correct by construction; `updateInterval(index,…)` becomes `updateStop(id, { easing })` — the same id-addressed door every other mutation already uses; the subject's emit becomes `"update-easing": [stopId: string, value: AuthoredEasing]`; useSpecimenRows derives rows by a pairwise walk over one array instead of zipping two.

defects.defect: Dead re-export shims that exist only to preserve import paths — 7 of 9 re-exported names have zero consumers, and the 2 live ones form a three-hop alias chain the sibling workbench crosses in one hop.

Measured outside the owning composables/ dir: `grep -rn "serializeCoalescedGradient|serializeRailRamp|linearInterval|parseGradientCSS|serializeGradient" demo/ … | grep -v composables/` → only two COMMENT hits (GradientStopEditor.vue:9, easingCatalogue.ts:44); `grep -rn "GradientParseResult|ParsedGradientModel" demo/ … | grep -v composables/` → no output. useGradientInterpolation.ts:13-17 re-exports INTERPOLATION_SPACES/HUE_INTERPOLATION_METHODS from color-session/color-space-meta with the comment "Re-exported here so the gradient tree's own consumers keep their import path". Chain: color-space-meta → useGradientInterpolation → useGradientModel → GradientVisualizer.vue:17-21. Sibling: demo/workbenches/mix/MixConfigBar.vue:18 imports the same constants from color-session/color-space-meta directly.
defects.mechanism: back-compat alias / dual path (owner edict 2: no aliases, migration shims, dual paths) — a re-export layer preserved for consumers that no longer exist.
defects.reproduction: Delete useGradientModel.ts:19-29 and useGradientInterpolation.ts:17, then repoint GradientVisualizer.vue:17-21 at ../../../color-session/color-space-meta. `npm run typecheck` passes — the greps above prove no other consumer exists.
defects.proposedCure: Delete both re-export blocks; import each concept from its single canonical home, as MixConfigBar.vue already does. Net −11 lines, one path per concept.

defects.defect: A leaf composable is imported from glass-ui's root barrel when a dedicated subpath publishes it, entering 21x more module graph; systemic across the demo, with three competing clipboard idioms alive.
defects.evidence: GradientEasingEditor.vue:29 `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui";` while it lives at dist/composables/dom/useClipboard.d.ts behind `"./dom"`. Measured first-hop weight: glass-ui.js imports 43 chunks / 168,303 bytes; dom.js imports 6 chunks / 7,876 bytes. Systemic: 37 root-barrel vs 82 subpath imports across demo/; all 15 clipboard import sites use the barrel and 0 use ./dom (greps in report). Three idioms: useClipboard at GradientEasingEditor.vue:94; writeClipboard with the CopyResult discarded at GradientVisualizer.vue:12,128 (same pane); raw `navigator.clipboard.writeText` at demo/picker/visual/PointerDebugOverlay.vue:112.
defects.mechanism: public-surface misuse — reaching a leaf through a package's aggregate entry, plus duplicate concept implementations for 'copy text with feedback'.
defects.reproduction: `grep -oE 'from *"\./[^"]+"' node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/glass-ui.js | sort -u | wc -l` → 43; same over dom.js → 6. Byte sums 168,303 vs 7,876.
defects.proposedCure: `import { useClipboard } from "@mkbabb/glass-ui/dom";` here, and one idiom per repo — `useClipboard` wherever a tick is shown, `writeClipboard` only where nothing is shown, never raw `navigator.clipboard`. Retire the 37 barrel imports to their subpaths.

defects.defect: The component re-implements two glass-ui 7.0.0 primitives that the demo already uses elsewhere — the disclosure accordion and the quiet icon button — and its child per-instance-overrides a design-system variant it is simultaneously requesting.
defects.evidence: Accordion hand-rolled at GradientEasingEditor.vue:61-71 + 117-147 (ref<number|null>, toggleInterval, hand-wired aria-expanded/aria-controls/id, v-show panel, manually rotated ChevronDown) vs glass-ui `Collapsible`/`CollapsibleTrigger`/`CollapsibleContent` (dist/components/collapsible/index.d.ts), already used at demo/workbenches/mix/MixSourceSelector.vue:181-226 with tokenized data-[state=open]:animate-collapsible-down transitions. Ghost icon buttons: 23 lines of scoped CSS at GradientEasingEditor.vue:269-291 vs glass-ui Button `emphasis?: "primary"|"secondary"|"quiet"|"text"`, `iconOnly?: boolean` (dist/components/button/Button.vue.d.ts:4-16), reachable via demo/ui/button and used by 22 demo files. Child: EasingSpecimenStrip.vue:163-170 re-declares display:flex/flex-direction:column/align-items/gap/padding on .specimen-tile — the exact geometry `shape="cell"` already applies (chipVariants.d.ts SHAPE.cell = "glass-chip--cell flex-col gap-1.5 px-2 py-2.5 text-micro").
defects.mechanism: second implementation of a concept that already has a home in the design system (owner edicts 4 and 5: glass-ui owns variants/primitives; style at the root component level, never per-instance).
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). Verified by presence: `grep -rn "Collapsible" demo/` → MixSourceSelector.vue uses it; `grep -rl "/ui/button" demo/` → 22 files use glass-ui Button; this component uses neither.
defects.proposedCure: `<Collapsible v-model:open>` per specimen row; `<Button emphasis="quiet" icon-only size="xs">` for the two rail controls; delete .rail-btn/.rail-btn--on and the accordion state. If the --motion-accent tinted 'on' state has no `tone` that expresses it, that is a glass-ui Button variant request — it belongs there, not in demo scoped CSS. Drop the .specimen-tile geometry block and let shape="cell" own it.

defects.defect: `easingValue` — the Result-unwrap-or-throw helper — exists twice, byte-identical but for its error string, in two modules already inside one import tree.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 and useGradientCSS.ts:71-77: identical signature `(result: ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>, source: string): EasingFunction` and identical body `if (result.ok) return result.value; throw new Error(...)` — only the message text differs. Both are also called with `steppedEase(...)` results (easingCatalogue.ts:137, useGradientCSS.ts:113), which only type-checks because the two Result shapes coincide.
defects.mechanism: duplicated ownership of one concept across two private homes.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). `grep -n -A7 "function easingValue" <both files>` shows the duplication verbatim.
defects.proposedCure: One `unwrapEasing(result, source)` beside the model — or better, export `unwrapOrThrow` from src/easing.ts, since throw-on-err is a library Result ergonomic, not a gradient fact.

defects.defect: Two placement conventions for composables inside one workbench: gradient composables at gradient/composables/*, easing composable+catalogue three levels deeper under a component-named directory — producing the tree's only four-level cross-feature reach.
defects.evidence: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/{gradientParse,useGradientCSS,useGradientInterpolation,useGradientModel}.ts vs demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/{easingCatalogue.ts,useSpecimenRows.ts}. Consequence: useSpecimenRows.ts:13 `import { useSafeAccentFn } from "../../../../color-session/useContrastSafeColor";` — the only `../../../../` in the workbench. The sibling `extract/` already follows the other rule (ImageEyedropper/{ImageEyedropper.vue,composables/}).
defects.mechanism: inconsistent module lattice — a component-named container directory used as a namespace, so co-located composables sit at a different depth than the feature's other composables.
defects.reproduction: NONE (structural). `grep -rn 'from "../../../..' demo/workbenches/gradient/` → one hit, useSpecimenRows.ts:13.
defects.proposedCure: Greenfield lattice, one rule — a feature directory owns its components AND its composables at the same depth: gradient/{model/, easing/, stops/, code/, GradientVisualizer.vue, GradientPane.vue}. GradientVisualizer/ as a container disappears; the deepest cross-feature reach becomes ../../color-session/… matching MixConfigBar.vue:18.

defects.defect: The specimen catalogue is built as a module-scope side effect, so 1,617 curve evaluations and 22.6 KB of retained SVG path strings are paid on gradient-pane open whether or not any easing row is ever expanded.
defects.evidence: easingCatalogue.ts:198 `export const SPECIMEN_FAMILIES: SpecimenFamily[] = buildFamilies();` — top level. Static import chain: easingCatalogue → GradientEasingEditor.vue:35 → GradientVisualizer.vue:16 → async GradientPane (demo/shell/usePaneRouter.ts:74). Measured against this repo's dist/subpaths/easing.js: tiles 33, build 3.02 ms cold / 1.77 ms avg warm, 22,651 bytes of path strings retained. glyphPath samples 49 points per curve (samples=48, i<=samples) with two toFixed(3) formats each → 1,617 evaluations, ~3,234 string formats.
defects.mechanism: eager module-scope evaluation of derived data in a leaf module — the catalogue is a pure function of the frozen library constant bezierPresets but is neither lazy nor build-time generated.
defects.reproduction: `node scratchpad/cat-bench.mjs` (the exact catalogue arithmetic against dist/subpaths/easing.js) → `tiles: 33 / build ms (cold): 3.02 / path-string bytes retained: 22651 / avg ms over 10 warm builds: 1.77`.
defects.proposedCure: Make SPECIMEN_FAMILIES a lazily-built module singleton (getter memoized on first strip mount), or generate it at build time as static data — it is a pure function of a frozen library constant, so both are free.
